backend.name: explicitly fake local Cloud KMS backend

distribution.reason: kms-integrations Apache-2.0 source plus linked BoringSSL (OpenSSL/ISC dual, MIT fiat), gRPC/Abseil/protobuf families and 86 Go modules are compiled into the shipped module/binaries without completed corresponding-source, notice or relinking delivery; whole-image licensing, toolchain reachability, generated layers and digest-bound source delivery remain incomplete. No publication authorized.

constraints: Linux amd64/glibc 2.41. Both channels build libkmsp11.so from source with Bazel 6.4.0 (-c opt --jobs 2 --copt=-Wno-error=discarded-qualifiers) from 35 sealed archives plus a pinned Go 1.22.0 SDK and 2 sealed Go zips for the host code generator, with downloads disabled; fakekms and the provisioning helper build with Go 1.27.1 from 86 sealed modules with GOPROXY=off. Four ordered P11Lab patches (SDK hash freeze, generated fault bindings, kms v1.25.0 floor, original helper); no prebuilt upstream bytes; the fake backend is explicit simulation.

Statically linked client: libkmsp11.so dynamically uses only Debian base libm/libc/libstdc++/libgcc (gcc 14.2); fakekms, the helper and the supervisor are static or libc/dl-only (CGO_ENABLED=0 Go, libc/dl C). No source-built system crypto, no openssl CLI, no Java/Maven, no compiler or Go toolchain in the runtime; ldd receipts identify actual usage.

Co-located supervised fakekms: one memory-only gRPC mock runs as a direct supervisor child for the operation/application lifetime. No permanent server/server-ready operation exists; the preferred proxy daemon uses the same supervised exec lifetime.

Ephemeral loopback topology: fakekms takes no arguments and prints an OS-ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port to stdout; the supervisor parses it strictly, then gates readiness on a real gRPC round-trip plus provisioning, never the printed address alone. Each independent shard/client owns its volume, container, PID namespace and network namespace; no host/shared networking.

Per-launch provisioning: every init/health/exec starts a fresh fakekms (zero keyrings) and provisions keyring projects/p/locations/global/keyRings/p11lab plus six SOFTWARE keys (RSA PKCS#1/PSS sign, EC P-256/P-384 sign, RSA OAEP decrypt, HMAC-SHA256), waiting for ENABLED versions. Provisioning recreates every key per launch, but upstream fakekms semantics are mixed: RSA keys are fixed pregenerated test vectors (rsaKeyFactory loads embedded testdata/rsa_*_private.pem, so the modulus repeats across launches), while EC and HMAC keys draw fresh crypto/rand material per launch (observed). All fake behavior, never real-KMS claims. No baked keys, credentials or initialized state ship.

P11LAB_LABEL defaults to P11Lab, 1..32 ASCII letters/digits/spaces/dot/underscore/hyphen. The label names the single token (slot 0, token-present index 0) via the generated 0600 libkmsp11 config; native flags are exactly 0x400409 and the mechanism roster is exactly 46 entries (24 zeros: 23 from an upstream vector-size mistake plus genuine CKM_RSA_PKCS_KEY_PAIR_GEN).

Caller PIN input is accepted for contract compatibility but ignored natively: C_Login(CKU_USER) succeeds with any value, even empty (empty is still refused at the adapter as malformed, matching the shared credential contract). No PIN ever reaches the supervisor; readiness never logs in.

No security-officer input exists: the token presents SO as PIN-locked and native C_Login(CKU_SO) is CKR_PIN_LOCKED (0xA4); C_InitToken/C_InitPIN/C_SetPIN/C_CreateObject are CKR_FUNCTION_NOT_SUPPORTED (0x54). P11LAB_SO_PIN/P11LAB_SO_PIN_FILE inputs are refused when set. C_GenerateKeyPair without the CKA_KMS_ALGORITHM vendor template fails: an empty template is CKR_TEMPLATE_INCOMPLETE (0xD0) and public-key attributes are CKR_TEMPLATE_INCONSISTENT (0xD1); general-token is falsified.

Vendor key generation works: C_GenerateKeyPair with CKA_LABEL plus CKA_KMS_ALGORITHM (and optional CKA_KMS_PROTECTION_LEVEL) creates a real key against the mock, and C_DestroyObject removes it. Duplicate labels fail natively (0x07). No retry, error translation or semantic patch is added.

Existing init validates static state and native readiness and ignores changed credential inputs. Static exact-byte marker checks, .init-lock, an exclusive volume lease, private control lock, ownership/mode/link/roster checks run before any native process. Missing, partial, foreign, incompatible and occupied state is refused. No reset, reprovisioning or state-changing retry is implicit.

init/health/exec use the P11Lab C supervisor: direct fakekms child, real readiness gating (owned PID, strict loopback port parse, TCP accept, bounded gRPC provisioning round-trip, native slot/label/flags/mechanism/object check), bounded startup and 64-KiB log sink, required-service death monitoring, signal forwarding, TERM/KILL escalation and subreaper/adopted-child cleanup.

Key material never survives restart (memory-only backend); the completion marker and label binding persist and re-validate. Reset is explicit caller removal/replacement of disposable state after all operations stop. Crash/power-loss recovery is unqualified.

Basic runtime contains no checker, Python, datasets, tracing, compiler, Bazel, Go toolchain, OpenSC/pkcs11-tool or upstream release binaries. Consumer/checker/proxy derivatives are separate test artifacts with independent identity and admission. A shared network never makes the native module remotely loadable.

kms-vendor-crypto means exactly the proven narrow observation: six pre-provisioned keys, vendor-template key generation, RSA PKCS#1/PSS and ECDSA P-256/P-384 signing, RSA-OAEP decrypt, HMAC-SHA256 and random generation, each with independent oracles, plus restart/isolation evidence. Wider mechanisms, key types, session objects, concurrent clients, other architectures/libcs and real Cloud KMS behavior are unqualified.

Distribution is blocked independently of crypto or lifecycle outcomes. Linked BoringSSL dual/MIT-fiat code, gRPC/Abseil/protobuf families and 86 Go modules have no completed corresponding-source, notice or relinking delivery; opencensus-proto carries no in-archive license text; base-package source obligations, toolchain reachability and actual-layer review remain pending.
